steps.name: Load, QC, and filter counts/metadata
caveats: n=3 per group is small; flag if any QC metric suggests a sample should be treated cautiously, but do not drop samples without clear justification
steps.context: Input files: /eval-four-models-without-star-counts-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 7: gene symbol column + 6 sample columns) and /eval-four-models-without-star-counts-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 rows x 2 columns: sample, condition). Counts are raw integers from STAR/featureCounts — no transcript-level quantification involved, so no tximport or effective-length correction is needed.
steps.question: Do the raw STAR/featureCounts gene counts (12000 genes x 6 samples) and the sample metadata (condition: treated vs control) align correctly, and which genes pass a minimum-expression filter before differential testing?
constraints: Do not apply any normalization at this stage beyond inspecting library sizes — normalization is DESeq2's internal responsibility in the next step
Treat gene symbol column as row names/identifiers, not a data column
acceptance_criteria: Sample names in counts.csv columns match sample IDs in metadata.csv rows exactly (order or explicit reindexing checked)
Confirms 3 treated and 3 control samples as stated in the design
Reports total genes before/after a low-count filter (e.g. require count >=10 in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size)
Outputs a filtered counts matrix and matched metadata table for downstream DESeq2 use
Reports basic library size per sample and flags any sample as an outlier if library size deviates >3x from the median

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: Small sample size limits power to detect modest effect sizes; do not overstate confidence in the exact gene list boundary
No paired structure or known confounders were reported — if metadata reveals additional variables (e.g. sex, sequencing lane) not currently listed, escalate rather than silently ignoring them
steps.context: Single batch, unpaired 3 vs 3 design (treated vs control) on liver tissue, raw integer STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts. No additional covariates (age, sex, batch) reported in metadata, so the model uses condition alone.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 profiled liver genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated (n=3) and control (n=3) samples, using a negative-binomial model on raw STAR/featureCounts counts?
constraints: Use raw filtered counts (not pre-normalized values) as DESeq2 input — DESeq2 performs its own size-factor normalization internally
Report both unshrunken and shrunken log2FoldChange; use the shrunken estimate for ranking/visualization
State explicitly that with n=3 per group, statistical power is limited and borderline (padj 0.05-0.1) genes should be interpreted cautiously
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 model specified as ~condition with condition releveled so control is the reference level
Wald test used for the treated-vs-control contrast; independent filtering (default DESeq2 behavior) applied on the results
Log2 fold-change shrinkage applied (apeglm or ashr) for a stable ranked gene list, given the small n=3/3 design
Output table includes gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for all filtered genes
Significant DE genes reported at padj < 0.05 (and separately a more permissive padj < 0.1 sensitivity check), with counts of up- vs down-regulated genes
PCA plot (on variance-stabilized/rlog-transformed data) and sample-distance heatmap produced to confirm treated/control separation and check for outliers or batch structure

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on the DE gene list
caveats: GO-BP results will show correlated/redundant blocks of significant terms due to ontology nesting — collapse or note this rather than presenting raw term counts as independent discoveries
Hallmark and WikiPathways sets are much smaller/coarser than GO-BP; interpret convergence across collections as stronger evidence than a hit in only one
steps.context: Gene identifiers in the counts matrix are human gene symbols (HGNC), matching the identifier space of the staged human pathway gene set files: MSigDB hallmark (50 sets), MSigDB GO-BP (7,538 sets), WikiPathways human (HGNC symbols), and MSigDB canonical pathways (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID, 1,146 sets total) — all confirmed present under the managed reference store for Homo sapiens.
steps.question: Which biological pathways and processes are over-represented among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
constraints: Match gene identifiers by symbol; do not attempt cross-species set matching
Use BH (Benjamini-Hochberg) multiple-testing correction consistently across collections
acceptance_criteria: Runs both an over-representation analysis (ORA) on significant DE genes (padj<0.05, split into up- and down-regulated) and a GSEA-style ranked analysis on the full gene list ranked by shrunken log2FoldChange (or DESeq2 stat)

Uses human-specific gene sets: MSigDB Hallmark, MSigDB GO Biological Process, WikiPathways human, and MSigDB canonical pathways (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID) — all confirmed present in the environment for Homo sapiens
Reports top enriched terms per collection with adjusted p-values (BH-corrected), gene ratios, and leading-edge/contributing genes
Explicitly notes GO-BP hierarchical redundancy (parent/child terms sharing members) rather than reporting raw term counts as independent findings
If the DE gene list from T2S1 is empty or very small (e.g., <10 genes at padj<0.05), reports this explicitly and falls back to reporting GSEA on the full ranked list only

plan.title: Liver drug treatment vs control DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq liver study with a simple 3 vs 3 unpaired, single-batch design (treated vs control), raw integer gene-level counts already produced by STAR/featureCounts (12000 genes x 6 samples in counts.csv, sample metadata in metadata.csv). Because counts come from featureCounts and not from a transcript-level quantifier (e.g. Salmon/kallisto), no tximport/gene-length-scaled-TPM step is needed or appropriate — the counts matrix goes directly into a count-based negative-binomial DE model. DESeq2 is the standard, well-supported tool for this (available in the sandbox) and handles the small n=3/3 design appropriately with its shrinkage estimators. The plan: (1) load and QC the counts/metadata, confirm sample-to-condition mapping and filter low-count genes; (2) run DESeq2 with condition (treated vs control) as the sole factor, given single batch and no other covariates reported, applying independent filtering, Wald test, and log2FC shrinkage (apeglm/ashr) for a robust ranked and thresholded gene list; (3) visualize results (volcano, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) for QC and interpretability; (4) run pathway enrichment (over-representation and/or GSEA) on the DE result using human hallmark, GO-BP, WikiPathways, and MSigDB canonical pathway gene sets staged in the environment, to give biological context to the DE gene list. No translational/clinical/PK data or explicit drug-target question is present in the research question beyond 'drug treatment' as a condition label, so no additional translational-safety or drug-repurposing steps are added speculatively.
